# Tauri Universal — Complete documentation



> Generated from the checked-in MDX documentation. Prefer `llms.txt` plus one relevant page when possible.



## Introduction

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/index.mdx`

This is the documentation index. It is built with [Fumadocs](https://fumadocs.dev) and TanStack Start. The site and its optional framework previews run on the same web domain.

## What's inside

- **Dashboard** — an overview of your todos
- **Todos** — create and manage tasks
- **Form blocks** — reusable form components

## Writing docs

Every `.mdx` file under `apps/docs/content/docs` becomes a page. Frontmatter controls its title and description.

## Agent Guide

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/agent.mdx`

Read the root `AGENTS.md` first. It is the authoritative operating contract. This page routes repository work; API facts come from the checked-in catalog and focused component pages.

## Start with one command

```bash
pnpm agent find table --framework vue
pnpm agent inspect ProDataTable --framework react
pnpm agent inspect block.data-table --framework react
pnpm agent recipe crud-page --framework react
pnpm agent budget --check
pnpm agent check --changed
```

`agent/catalog.json` is the machine-readable capability source. `/llms.txt` is the standard documentation index, `/llms-full.txt` is the optional complete bundle, and `/docs/<path>.md` exposes clean Markdown for one page. Prefer the index plus one relevant page over the full bundle.

## Workspace map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/pro-core` | Framework-free form, table, and query contracts |
| `packages/ui` | React DOM primitives and CSS design tokens |
| `packages/pro` | React feature blocks |
| `packages/pro-vue` | Vue feature-block adapters |
| `packages/pro-svelte` | Svelte feature-block adapters |
| `packages/ui-native` | React Native/Web primitives styled with Uniwind (Tailwind classes, shared tokens.css) |
| `packages/tauri-api` | Typed Tauri operations and browser fallbacks |
| `packages/core` | Shared application domain logic |
| `packages/cli` | Agent discovery, verification, and scaffold commands |
| `apps/*-playground` | Compileable integration examples for each framework |

## Hard conventions

1. Use stable package subpaths such as `@package/ui/button`; legacy `src/*` imports are compatibility-only. Do not add root barrel files.
2. Put framework-neutral contracts in `pro-core` before adapters.
3. Keep raw Tauri calls inside `tauri-api` and provide a browser fallback.
4. Register new Tailwind-scanned package sources in each consuming app stylesheet.
5. Add component/block docs and catalog metadata with the implementation.
6. Use shadcn patterns for primitives and TanStack engines for feature blocks.

## Safe scaffolding

```bash
pnpm scaffold list
pnpm scaffold add ui alert --dry-run
pnpm scaffold add ui alert
```

Only complete vendored templates are accepted by default. Unknown components fail without writing. `--allow-placeholder` is an explicit escape hatch and is not production-ready. Use `--no-install` to plan dependency changes separately and `--json` for machine-readable output.

## Documentation maintenance

Run `pnpm agent:docs` after documentation or catalog changes. `pnpm agent:docs:check` detects stale checked-in `llms.txt` artifacts without writing. The normal changed-scope verifier includes this check.

## Known operational details

- `pnpm dev` starts the browser frontend; `pnpm tauri dev` starts the native shell.
- Fumadocs type generation runs when the docs app starts or builds.
- Sidebar order comes from each folder's `meta.json`.
- `pnpm agent check --changed` selects affected framework builds and prints detailed output only on failure.

## Architecture

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/architecture.mdx`

## Workspace layout

| Path | Purpose |
| ---- | ------- |
| `apps/docs` | TanStack Start + React DOM Kitchen and documentation site |
| `packages/core` | Shared business logic |
| `packages/ui` | Shared UI components (shadcn-based) |
| `packages/pro` | Pro layout components |
| `packages/tauri-api` | Typed Tauri command bindings for separate native app consumers |

## Tech stack

- **TanStack Start** for the browser application and route rendering
- **TanStack Router** for typed routing
- **TanStack Query** for data fetching
- **Tailwind CSS v4** for styling
- **Fumadocs** for this documentation section

## Data flow

The Kitchen Todo example stores its data in browser local storage and exposes it through TanStack Query hooks in `src/lib/todo-queries.ts`. The optional Vue, Svelte, and React Native Web + UniWind examples are separate same-origin bundles that load after selection.

## Pro Core

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/pro-core.mdx`

`@package/pro-core` holds the **framework-free contracts** that pro component adapters consume. It has no React, Vue, or Svelte dependencies — only types and pure functions — which is what lets the same contracts drive adapters across frameworks.

There is no package-root entrypoint; import each module by its full path:

```bash
@package/pro-core/form
@package/pro-core/table
@package/pro-core/table-features
@package/pro-core/table-engine
@package/pro-core/query
```

## Form schema

`form/schema` defines the declarative form model rendered by `ProForm` adapters (`ProFormDialog` in React):

- `ProFieldSchema` — one field: `name`, `label`, `type` (`text | textarea | number | select | checkbox | switch`), plus `placeholder`, `description`, `options`, `required`, `disabled`, and synchronous `validators` (functions returning an error message or `undefined`).
- `ProFormGroup` — fields grouped under a shared `title`/`description` with a `stacked` or `grid-2` layout.
- `validateField(schema, raw)` — runs the required check, then every validator, returning the first error.

```ts

const title = {
  name: 'text',
  label: 'Task',
  type: 'text',
  required: true,
} as const;

validateField(title, ''); // "Task is required"
```

## Column DSL

`table/columns` is the declarative column model for pro data tables. Adapters map each `valueType` to a concrete cell renderer:

| ValueType | Renders |
| --------- | ------- |
| `text` / `number` / `date` | Plain values, dates via locale formatting |
| `badge` / `status` | `@package/ui` badge variants |
| `actions` | Row action buttons from an `onSelect(row)` list |

Useful members: `ProColumnDef<T>` (the union), `isActionColumn()` (type guard), and `readCellValue(row, column)` which resolves the `accessor` (defaulting to `key`).

```ts

const columns: Array<ProColumnDef<TodoRow>> = [
  { key: 'text', header: 'Task', valueType: 'text' },
  { key: 'priority', header: 'Priority', valueType: 'badge', hiddenByDefault: true },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', valueType: 'status' },
  {
    key: 'actions',
    header: '',
    valueType: 'actions',
    actions: [
      { label: 'Done', onSelect: (row) => toggle(row.id) },
      { label: 'Delete', destructive: true, onSelect: (row) => remove(row.id) },
    ],
  },
];
```

## Table features & query contract

`table/features` configures which capabilities a table instance exposes and defines the server-mode contract:

- `TableFeatures` — toggles for `sorting`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `refresh`, plus `pageSizeOptions`.
- `TableQuery` / `PagedResult<T>` — the shape adapters translate into their fetcher when a table runs in **server mode**; in client mode everything happens in memory.
- `buildTableQuery({ page, pageSize, ... })` — normalizes a query with `undefined` defaults for the optional fields.

```ts

buildTableQuery({ page: 0, pageSize: 20 });
// { page: 0, pageSize: 20, sortBy: undefined, sortDir: undefined, search: undefined }
```

## Client engine

`table/client-engine` is the in-memory pipeline for lightweight adapters (Svelte today): `filterRows` (case-insensitive search across non-action columns), `sortRows` (numeric-aware, stable copy), and `pageRows`. Each step takes the output of the previous one, so adapters compose them freely.

## Query keys

`query/keys` provides deterministic cache-key factories shared by every adapter, so mutations invalidate consistently across frameworks:

```ts

queryKeys.table('todos', { page: 0 }); // ['pro', 'table', 'todos', { page: 0 }]
queryKeys.detail('todos', 1); //        ['pro', 'detail', 'todos', 1]
queryKeys.stats('todos'); //            ['pro', 'stats', 'todos']
```

Invalidation can use the key prefix — this app's todo mutations invalidate `['pro', 'table', 'todos']`, which matches every parameterization of `queryKeys.table('todos', …)`.

## Blocks

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/index.mdx`

**Blocks** are higher-level feature components: complete, composable units (a searchable sortable table, a schema-driven form, an app shell) assembled from UI primitives, `@package/pro-core` contracts, and TanStack engines. React implementations live in `@package/pro`; Vue and Svelte adapters implement the same contracts in `@package/pro-vue` and `@package/pro-svelte`.

## The blocks

| Block | Purpose |
| ----- | ------- |
| `ProCrudPage` | Config-first controlled CRUD page; the shortest path for standard resource screens |
| `ProDataTable` | Toolbar + table + pagination over TanStack Table, client or server mode |
| `ProForm` | Schema-driven form over TanStack Form with validation and submit states |
| `ProFormDialog` | ProForm inside a Dialog for create/edit flows |
| `AppShell` | Application frame: sidebar nav, header, content area |
| `PageContainer` | Breadcrumb trail, title block, actions, page body |

## Block vs. component

Components (`@package/ui`) are dumb primitives — a Button, an Input. Blocks own **behavior and data plumbing**: ProDataTable wires sorting/filter/pagination state, ProForm runs validation and submit lifecycles. Rule of thumb from the README: *blocks are shadcn primitives + TanStack engines only*, no other state or data libraries.

## Where they're used

- `/todos` — compact `ProCrudPage` resource definition for task management
- `/forms` — `ProForm` showcase with validation, groups, and submit states
- Everywhere — `AppShell` wraps the app (see `src/routes.tsx`), `PageContainer` wraps each page

## ProCrudPage

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-crud-page.mdx`

`ProCrudPage` composes the page container, data table, form dialog, and delete confirmation. The app keeps ownership of fetching and mutations through a typed controller.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage

```tsx
const tasks = defineProResource<Task, { text: string }>({
  id: 'tasks', title: 'Tasks', getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  columns: [{ key: 'text', header: 'Task', valueType: 'text' }],
  form: {
    schema: [{ fields: [{ name: 'text', label: 'Task', type: 'text', required: true }] }],
    create: { title: 'New task', values: { text: '' } },
  },
});

<ProCrudPage resource={tasks} controller={{ rows, create, remove }} />;
```

## Contract

- The controller supplies rows, loading/error state, refresh, and optional create/update/remove callbacks.
- The block adds actions only for callbacks that exist and confirms destructive deletes.
- `headerActions`, `toolbar`, `empty`, and `footer` accept React nodes for customization.
- Rejected mutations stay open and render their error; React Query or another data layer remains app-owned.

## ProDataTable

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-data-table.mdx`

A complete list view: search toolbar, column sorting, column visibility, page-size selector, pagination, loading/error/empty states. Source: `packages/pro/src/data-table/pro-data-table.tsx`, built on **TanStack Table v9** (`useTable` + `tableFeatures` with registered sorting/filtering/pagination/selection/visibility features) and `@package/ui` table primitives. Column shape comes from the `ProColumnDef` DSL in `@package/pro-core`.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage


```tsx title="Client mode (from src/pages/todos-page.tsx)"

const columns: Array<ProColumnDef<TodoRow>> = [
  { key: 'text', header: 'Task', valueType: 'text' },
  { key: 'createdAt', header: 'Created', valueType: 'date' },
  {
    key: 'actions',
    header: '',
    valueType: 'actions',
    actions: [
      { label: 'Done', onSelect: (row) => toggle(row.id) },
      { label: 'Delete', destructive: true, onSelect: (row) => remove(row.id) },
    ],
  },
];

<ProDataTable columns={columns} data={todos} loading={isLoading} />
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ----- |
| `columns` | `Array<ProColumnDef<T>>` | Column DSL from `@package/pro-core`. |
| `data` | `T[]` | Row data for client mode. |
| `loading` / `error` / `onRetry` | — | State rendering: skeletons, error card with retry. |
| `features` | `TableFeatures` | Toggle sorting, globalFilter, pagination, rowSelection, columnVisibility, refresh. |
| `query` + `totalRows` + `onQueryChange` | `TableQuery` | **Server mode**: pass all three and the table stops managing state internally; your fetcher owns the data. |
| `searchPlaceholder`, `toolbarExtra`, `onRefresh` | — | Toolbar customization. |
| `getRowId` | `(row) => string` | Stable row identity for selection. |

## Client vs. server mode

Without `query`, filtering/sorting/pagination happen in memory (TanStack row models). Pass `query`/`totalRows`/`onQueryChange` and the block becomes a controlled view over your API — translate `TableQuery` into fetch parameters and feed back rows + total. Pair it with `queryKeys.table()` from `@package/pro-core` so cache invalidation stays deterministic.

## ProDescriptions

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-descriptions.mdx`

Display structured record details and entity summaries with columns, border grids, and schema-driven rendering. Source: `packages/pro/src/descriptions/pro-descriptions.tsx`.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage

```tsx

const record = {
  id: 'usr_102',
  username: 'antigravity',
  role: 'Maintainer',
  active: true,
  createdAt: '2026-09-19',
};

<ProDescriptions
  title="User Overview"
  bordered
  column={2}
  data={record}
>
  <ProDescriptionsItem label="ID" dataIndex="id" valueType="code" />
  <ProDescriptionsItem label="Username" dataIndex="username" />
  <ProDescriptionsItem label="Role" dataIndex="role" valueType="badge" />
  <ProDescriptionsItem label="Active" dataIndex="active" valueType="boolean" />
</ProDescriptions>
```

## API

| Prop | Values | Default |
| ---- | ------ | ------- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `undefined` |
| `extra` | `ReactNode` | `undefined` |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `column` | `1` \| `2` \| `3` \| `4` | `3` |
| `layout` | `horizontal` \| `vertical` | `horizontal` |
| `data` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` |
| `schema` | `ProFieldSchema[]` | `undefined` |
| `items` | `ProDescriptionsItemConfig[]` | `undefined` |

## ProFilterToolbar

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-filter-toolbar.mdx`

A collapsible search and filtering toolbar designed to connect directly with table queries and server filters.

---

## Installation

<Tabs items={['CLI', 'Manual']}>
  <Tab value="CLI">
```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli add pro-filter-toolbar
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Manual">
Import from `@package/pro/filter-toolbar`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Anatomy

```tsx

  return (
    <ProFilterToolbar
      fields={[
        { name: 'query', label: 'Search Keyword', type: 'text', placeholder: 'Search users...' },
        {
          name: 'role',
          label: 'Role',
          type: 'select',
          options: [
            { label: 'Admin', value: 'admin' },
            { label: 'User', value: 'user' },
            { label: 'Guest', value: 'guest' },
          ],
        },
        { name: 'date', label: 'Registered Date', type: 'date' },
        { name: 'window', label: 'Billing Period', type: 'date-range' },
      ]}
      onFilter={(filters) => {
        console.log('Applied filters:', filters);
      }}
      onReset={() => {
        console.log('Filters reset');
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

---

## Field types

`type` is one of `text`, `select`, `date`, or `date-range`. A `date-range` field renders a
`DateRangePicker` and stores a `[Date, Date]` tuple in the emitted filters; a value that is not a
two-`Date` tuple — for example two strings from a query string — is ignored and the control falls back
to its placeholder instead of throwing.

## ProForm

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-form.mdx`

Renders a complete form from a `ProFormGroup[]` schema (see `@package/pro-core/form`): field controls per type, synchronous validators, group titles/descriptions, `stacked` or `grid-2` layouts, pending state on submit. Source: `packages/pro/src/form/pro-form.tsx`, built on TanStack Form.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage


```tsx title="Schema-driven form"

const schema = [
  {
    title: 'Task details',
    fields: [
      { name: 'text', label: 'Task', type: 'text', required: true, placeholder: 'What needs doing?' },
      { name: 'notes', label: 'Notes', type: 'textarea', placeholder: 'Optional details…' },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: 'Options',
    layout: 'grid-2',
    fields: [
      { name: 'priority', label: 'Priority', type: 'select', options: [
        { label: 'Low', value: 'low' },
        { label: 'Normal', value: 'normal' },
        { label: 'High', value: 'high' },
      ] },
      { name: 'pinned', label: 'Pin to top', type: 'switch' },
    ],
  },
];

<ProForm
  schema={schema}
  defaultValues={{ priority: 'normal', pinned: false }}
  submitLabel='Create task'
  onSubmit={async (values) => {
    await addTodo(String(values.text));
  }}
/>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ----- |
| `schema` | `Array<ProFormGroup>` | Groups → fields; field types: `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `select`, `checkbox`, `switch`. |
| `defaultValues` | `ProFormValues` | Initial values keyed by field `name`. |
| `onSubmit` | `(values) => Promise<void> \| void` | Receives the collected values. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | Renders a Cancel button when provided. |
| `submitLabel` / `cancelLabel` | `string` | Button labels. |
| `pending` | `boolean` | Disables the submit button while true. |
| `className` | `string` | Extra classes on the form element. |

Validators are plain functions on the field schema (`validators: [(v) => v.length < 3 ? 'Too short' : undefined]`) — no schema library involved.

## ProFormDialog

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/pro-form-dialog.mdx`

Controlled Dialog wrapping `ProForm` — the standard create/edit surface. Key the rendered dialog by the edited record so defaults reset between opens. Source: `packages/pro/src/form/pro-form-dialog.tsx`.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage


```tsx title="Create flow (from src/pages/todos-page.tsx)"
const [createOpen, setCreateOpen] = useState(false);
const addTodo = useAddTodo();

<Button onClick={() => setCreateOpen(true)}>New task</Button>
<ProFormDialog
  open={createOpen}
  onOpenChange={setCreateOpen}
  title='New task'
  schema={createSchema}
  defaultValues={{}}
  submitLabel='Create'
  pending={addTodo.isPending}
  onSubmit={async (values) => {
    await addTodo.mutateAsync(String(values.text));
    setCreateOpen(false);
  }}
/>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ----- |
| `open` / `onOpenChange` | boolean / `(open) => void` | Controlled dialog visibility. |
| `title` / `description` | `string` | Dialog header text. |
| `schema` | `Array<ProFormGroup>` | Same schema as `ProForm`. |
| `defaultValues` | `ProFormValues` | Re-key the dialog element per record so values reset. |
| `onSubmit` | `(values) => Promise<void> \| void` | Close the dialog yourself after success. |
| `submitLabel` / `pending` | — | Submit button label and pending state. |

```tsx
    <ProFormDrawer
      title="Create Workspace"
      description="Configure workspace details and settings."

        {
          title: 'General',
          fields: [
            { name: 'name', label: 'Workspace Name', type: 'text', required: true },
            { name: 'slug', label: 'Slug', type: 'text', required: true },
          ],
        },
      ]}
      defaultValues={{ name: '', slug: '' }}
      onSubmit={async (values) => {
        console.log('Submitted', values);
        return true; // Closes drawer on success
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## AppShell

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/blocks/app-shell.mdx`

The application frame used by every route in this app: fixed-width sidebar with nav items (desktop), horizontal scrollable nav in the header (mobile), sticky header with the app title. Source: `packages/pro/src/layout/app-shell.tsx`. You are looking at it right now — this docs page renders inside the AppShell.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage

```tsx title="Root route (from src/routes.tsx)"

<AppShell
  title='Universal Todos'
  navItems={[
    { label: 'Dashboard', to: '/', icon: LayoutDashboardIcon },
    { label: 'Todos', to: '/todos', icon: ListTodoIcon },
    { label: 'Docs', to: '/docs', icon: BookOpenIcon },
  ]}
>
</AppShell>
```

## API

| Prop | Type | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ----- |
| `title` | `string` | Sidebar brand text and header title. |
| `navItems` | `Array<NavItem>` | `{ label, to, icon? }`; active state derives from `location.pathname` (exact or prefix match). |
| `headerExtra` | `ReactNode` | Right-aligned header slot (actions, theme toggle, …). |
| `sidebarAction` | `ReactNode` | Right-aligned slot in the sidebar title row. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Routed content. |

Active styling uses the `primary` background for the matched item; icons come from `lucide-react`.

| Prop | Type | Notes |

| `extra` | `ReactNode` | Right-aligned action slot beside the title. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | Below the body. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Page body. |

## Accordion

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/accordion.mdx`

Displays an accordion: vertically stacked, collapsible section panels. Source: `packages/ui/src/components/ui/accordion.tsx`, built on `@radix-ui/react-accordion`.

## Import

```ts
  Accordion,
  AccordionContent,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
} from '@package/ui/accordion';
```

## Usage


```tsx title="Example"
  Accordion,
  AccordionContent,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionTrigger,
} from '@package/ui/accordion';

  return (
    <Accordion type='single' collapsible>
      <AccordionItem value='item-1'>
        <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Yes. It uses Radix UI primitives with full keyboard and screen-reader support.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value='item-2'>
        <AccordionTrigger>Is it animated?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>
          Yes. Height animations come from the `accordion-down` / `accordion-up` keyframes
          defined in the shared theme tokens.
        </AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  );
}
```

## API

| Component | Props | Notes |
| --------- | ----- | ----- |
| `Accordion` | `type='single' \| 'multiple'`, `collapsible`, `defaultValue` | Root; forwarded to Radix Root. `type='single'` keeps one panel open; `collapsible` allows closing it. |
| `AccordionItem` | `value` (required) | One panel row; bottom border, no border on the last item. |
| `AccordionTrigger` | children | Header button with rotating chevron; `data-state=open` flips it 180°. |
| `AccordionContent` | children | Animated open/close wrapper; add padding via `className` on inner `div`. |

All props not listed are forwarded to the underlying Radix primitive, so `onValueChange`, `disabled`, and friends work as documented by Radix UI.

## Calendar

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/calendar.mdx`

A fast date picker calendar grid with month navigation and day selection without external date libraries.

---

## Installation

<Tabs items={['CLI', 'Manual']}>
  <Tab value="CLI">
```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli add calendar
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Manual">
Copy `calendar.tsx` to your components directory and import from `@package/ui/calendar` or `@package/ui-native`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Anatomy

```tsx

  const [date, setDate] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date());

  return (
    <Calendar
      value={date}
      onValueChange={setDate}
    />
  );
}
```

---

## Range mode

`mode="range"` renders a continuous span instead of a single day. The calendar stays presentational:
it reports day presses through `onSelect` and pointer movement through `onHoverChange`, and marks each
day with `data-range="start" | "middle" | "end"`. Anchor, preview, and bound handling live in the
shared `useRangeSelection` hook from `@package/ui/use-range-selection`, which is also what
`DateRangePicker` is built on.

```tsx

  const selection = useRangeSelection({ onSelect: (range) => console.log(range) });

  return (
    <Calendar
      mode="range"
      selected={selection.selected}
      preview={selection.preview}
      anchor={selection.anchor}
      onSelect={selection.press}
      onHoverChange={selection.hover}
    />
  );
}
```

Reach for `DateRangePicker` when a formatted trigger and popover are wanted; use the calendar directly
when the grid is the layout.

---

## Localization

Labels are formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, so the component stays zero-dependency. The heading,
weekday names, and each day's screen-reader label follow the runtime locale by default; the `locale`
prop pins one instead:

```tsx
<Calendar
  value={date}
  onValueChange={setDate}
  locale="fr-FR"
/>
```

Only the names localize. The grid stays Sunday-first, with day columns indexed by `getDay()`, so the
week layout does not shift between locales. `DatePicker` and `DateRangePicker` forward the same prop to
their trigger text and their calendar.

## Date Range Picker

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/date-range-picker.mdx`

A range input control rendering a formatted trigger button that opens a calendar selection popover and commits a `[from, to]` tuple.

---

## Installation

<Tabs items={['CLI', 'Manual']}>
  <Tab value="CLI">
```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli add date-range-picker
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Manual">
Copy `date-range-picker.tsx` and `calendar.tsx` to your components directory and import from `@package/ui/date-range-picker`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Anatomy

```tsx

  const [range, setRange] = useState<[Date, Date] | undefined>();

  return (
    <DateRangePicker
      value={range}
      onValueChange={setRange}
      placeholder="Select billing period..."
    />
  );
}
```

The first day press anchors the range and previews the span under the pointer; the second press commits
it and closes the popover. A press before the anchor swaps the ends instead of producing a backwards
range, and `onValueChange` receives `undefined` when the range is cleared.

---

## Bounds

`min` and `max` bound the committed span in whole days, both inclusive. The anchor stays fixed and the
other end is extended or trimmed to satisfy the bound. `excludeDisabled` trims the range at the first
day rejected by `disabledDate` rather than including it, and wins when both rules apply.

```tsx
<DateRangePicker
  value={range}
  onValueChange={setRange}
  min={2}
  disabledDate={(day) => day.getDay() === 0 || day.getDay() === 6}
  excludeDisabled
/>
```

`disabledDate` also receives the anchor as its second argument, so rules such as "no end before the
anchor" can be expressed directly.

---

## Dismiss behavior

`commitBehavior` decides what dismissing the popover mid-selection does, after the start day but
before the end day. `'reset'` (the default) discards the pick, `'clear'` clears the value, and
`'select'` commits the start day alone. A plain open-and-close is unaffected.

---

## Localization

The trigger text and the calendar labels are formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — no date library is
involved — so they follow the runtime locale. Pass `locale` to pin one:

```tsx
<DateRangePicker
  value={range}
  onValueChange={setRange}
  locale="fr-FR"
/>
```

Only the names localize; the day grid stays Sunday-first.

---

## Native

`@package/ui-native` ships the same component over the React Native `Modal`, with `style` instead of
`className` and without `id`. Both surfaces share the selection logic and day-state helpers from
`@package/ui/use-range-selection`, so range semantics stay identical across platforms.

## Interactive Drawer

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/drawer-interactive.mdx`

A mobile bottom sheet that executes worklets directly on the native UI thread, allowing interactive dragging with velocity-based flick dismiss and rubber-banding.

---

## Installation

<Tabs items={['CLI', 'Manual']}>
  <Tab value="CLI">
```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli add drawer-interactive --framework native
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Manual">
Install peer dependencies `react-native-reanimated` and `react-native-gesture-handler`, then copy `drawer-interactive.tsx`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Anatomy

```tsx
  InteractiveDrawer,
  InteractiveDrawerClose,
  InteractiveDrawerContent,
  InteractiveDrawerDescription,
  InteractiveDrawerFooter,
  InteractiveDrawerHeader,
  InteractiveDrawerTitle,
} from '@package/ui-native/drawer-interactive';

  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Open Interactive Sheet</Button>
      <InteractiveDrawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <InteractiveDrawerHeader>
          <InteractiveDrawerTitle>Interactive Bottom Sheet</InteractiveDrawerTitle>
          <InteractiveDrawerDescription>
            Drag down to dismiss or flick with downward velocity.
          </InteractiveDrawerDescription>
        </InteractiveDrawerHeader>
        <InteractiveDrawerFooter>
          <InteractiveDrawerClose>
            <Button variant="outline">Close</Button>
          </InteractiveDrawerClose>
        </InteractiveDrawerFooter>
      </InteractiveDrawer>
    </>
  );
}
```

---

## Key Features

- **120 FPS UI Thread**: Animation worklets execute directly on native thread via JSI.
- **Physical Gestures**: Pan gesture tracking with upward resistance rubber-banding.
- **Velocity Dismiss**: Automatically detects a downward flick velocity above 600 px/s to dismiss
  smoothly.


## API

`Table` wraps content in a horizontally scrollable container. `TableRow` highlights on hover; `TableRow` also accepts `data-state='selected'` for row-selection styling used by the pro table.

## Tabs

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/tabs.mdx`

A tabbed interface. Source: `packages/ui/src/components/ui/tabs.tsx`, built on `@radix-ui/react-tabs`.

## Import

```ts
```

## Usage


```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue='preview'>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value='preview'>Preview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='code'>Code</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value='preview'>…rendered output…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='code'>…source…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

## API

`Tabs` root (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `orientation`). Each `TabsTrigger` value must match a `TabsContent` value; only the active content is mounted.

## Toast

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/components/toast.mdx`

A responsive, stackable toast notification system inspired by Sonner with zero runtime styling overhead.

---

## Installation

<Tabs items={['CLI', 'Manual']}>
  <Tab value="CLI">
```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli add toast
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="Manual">
Copy `toast.tsx` to your components directory and import from `@package/ui/toast` or `@package/ui-native`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Anatomy

```tsx

  return (
    <>
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast.success('Record created', {
            description: 'Item has been added to your workspace.',
            action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => console.log('Undo') },
          })
        }
      >
        Show Toast
      </Button>

      {/* Render once at root layout */}
      <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
    </>
  );
}
```

---

## Key Features

- **Cross-Platform**: Zero-dependency GPU compositor transitions on Web; native driver springs on React Native.
- **Convenience Methods**: `toast()`, `toast.success()`, `toast.error()`, `toast.warning()`, `toast.info()`, `toast.dismiss()`.
- **Action Buttons**: Embedded callback buttons that automatically dismiss on press.

## Vue

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/platforms/vue.mdx`

The pro block layer ships a Vue adapter, `@package/pro-vue`: the same layout, form, and data-table blocks from the React docs re-implemented as single-file components that share the exact same design tokens (`@package/ui/tokens.css`).

## Blocks

| Block | File |
| ----- | ---- |
| AppShell | `packages/pro-vue/src/layout/app-shell.vue` |
| PageContainer | `packages/pro-vue/src/layout/page-container.vue` |
| ProForm | `packages/pro-vue/src/form/pro-form.vue` |
| ProFormDialog | `packages/pro-vue/src/form/pro-form-dialog.vue` |
| ProDataTable | `packages/pro-vue/src/data-table/pro-data-table.vue` |

The SFCs mirror the React prop APIs 1:1 so the blocks stay swappable behind a shared contract, and shared logic (filters, sorting, validation) comes from the framework-agnostic `@package/pro-core`.

## Running the playground

`apps/vue-playground` is a Vite + `@vitejs/plugin-vue` app that renders every block (forms view, todos view) on top of TanStack Vue Query:

```bash
pnpm --filter @app/vue-playground dev   # → http://localhost:1451
```

Its CSS entry imports the shared `tokens.css` and scans the Vue packages via `@source`, exactly like the React docs app does.

```bash
pnpm --filter @app/svelte-playground dev   # → http://localhost:1452
```

Its CSS entry imports the shared `tokens.css` and scans the Svelte packages via `@source`, exactly like the React docs app does.

## React Native Web

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/platforms/react-native-web.mdx`

The same Apple-inspired design system that powers the DOM components runs on **React Native Web (RNW)** via `@package/ui-native` — hand-built RN primitives (`Pressable`/`View`/`Text`) styled with **Uniwind**, which compiles Tailwind v4 classes for React Native at build time. No Metro, no Expo required: the playground is a plain Vite app.

## How it fits the adapter architecture

The repo's cross-framework recipe applies unchanged:

| Layer | DOM (React) | Native (RNW) |
| ----- | ----------- | ------------ |
| Tokens | `packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` (CSS custom properties) | **same file**, imported into the playground CSS entry |
| Components | `packages/ui` (Radix + Tailwind classes) | `packages/ui-native` (RN primitives + Uniwind `className`) |
| Playground | `apps/docs/previews/uniwind` (built on demand at `/previews/uniwind/`) | `apps/native-playground` (`vite-plugin-rnw` + `@tailwindcss/vite` + `uniwind/vite`, port 1453) |

## Uniwind styling

`apps/docs/previews/uniwind/vite.config.ts` chains `rnw()` (React Native Web resolution + fixes), `tailwindcss()`, and `uniwind({ cssEntryFile: './src/index.css' })`. Its CSS entry imports `tailwindcss`, `uniwind`, and the shared tokens, and scans `packages/ui-native/src` via `@source`. The preview is built separately and fetched only when selected; it runs in the browser through React Native Web, not on an iOS or Android device.

Components mirror the DOM siblings' class strings 1:1; color utilities (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `dark:bg-card`, …) resolve the tokens.css variables. Because RN has no style inheritance, container utilities sit on the primitive and text color/size utilities on the inner `Text` — see the `variantClasses` maps in `packages/ui-native/src/components/ui/*`. Web-only utilities (hover, focus rings) are elided; pressed feedback uses `active:`.

Dark mode is uniwind-managed: `Uniwind.setTheme('dark' | 'light')` flips the theme and uniwind keeps `<html class="dark">` in sync, so the tokens.css variables and every `dark:` variant switch together. The initial theme follows the system (uniwind's `adaptiveThemes` default). The toggle in `apps/native-playground/src/playground.tsx` is the reference implementation.

`packages/ui/src/tokens.ts` (the JS palette/shadow mirror) stays in the repo for future real-native Metro targets, but ui-native no longer imports it.

## Running the playground

```bash
pnpm dev:native   # standalone playground → http://localhost:1453
```

Renders every ui-native component (buttons in all variants/sizes, badges, a form card with Input + Switch, separators) with a working light/dark toggle.

## Component parity

| Primitive | Status | Notes |
| --------- | ------ |-------|
| Button | ✅ | All 6 variants + 4 sizes; same variant classes as the DOM version; `Pressable` |
| Badge | ✅ | 6 variants with the DOM tinted fills (`bg-primary/12`, `bg-green/15`, …) |
| Card | ✅ | All five slots (`Card`…`CardFooter`); `shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]` |
| Input | ✅ | Wraps RN `TextInput`; `invalid` prop mirrors `aria-invalid`; placeholder color via uniwind `useCSSVariable` |
| Switch | ✅ | Radix-style `checked`/`onCheckedChange` API; green-on track like the DOM version |
| Separator | ✅ | Horizontal/vertical hairline |
| Label | ✅ | Text port; pairs with `InputLabel` for form fields |
| Checkbox | ✅ | `checked`/`onCheckedChange` API; ✓ glyph indicator |
| Skeleton | ✅ | RN `Animated` pulse loop (Uniwind has no keyframes) |
| Textarea | ✅ | Multiline `TextInput` in a bordered box; token-aware placeholder |
| Table | ✅ | Rows become flex Views in a horizontal `ScrollView` |
| Accordion | ✅ | Context-based single-open list; `defaultValue` uncontrolled mode |
| Tabs | ✅ | Segmented `TabsList` + content panel; controlled or `defaultValue` |
| Tooltip | ✅ | Single `content`-prop API: press-and-hold shows the bubble |
| Dialog | ✅ | RN `Modal` card over a dimmed backdrop; `open`/`onOpenChange` |
| Dropdown Menu | ✅ | `Modal` action sheet; items, labels, separators, checkbox items |
| Popover | ✅ | `Modal` panel with arbitrary content; backdrop-press dismiss |
| Select | ✅ | `Modal` sheet; `value`/`onValueChange` with `SelectValue`/`SelectItem` markers |

RN has no portals or Radix, so the overlay components (Dialog, Dropdown Menu, Popover, Select) render via RN's `Modal` as centered sheets over a dimmed backdrop instead of anchored popups — the prop APIs stay DOM-compatible. lucide icons are replaced with text glyphs (✓ ⌄ ×) to avoid a `react-native-svg` dependency, and animations that rely on CSS keyframes (`animate-pulse`) use RN's `Animated` instead.

## Porting recipe (and the CLI)

New native components follow the DOM siblings' prop APIs so the two stay swappable behind a shared contract:

```bash
pnpm scaffold add native <kebab-name>   # emits from templates/native/, wires docs
```

The scaffold's `native` target writes to `packages/ui-native/src/components/ui/` and rewrites `@/lib/cn` → `@package/ui/cn`. Then port the real implementation from the DOM component: the Tailwind classes carry over as-is (Uniwind compiles them for RN), replace Radix behavior with RN primitives, and split text color/size utilities onto the `Text` node.

## Bare React Native (Uniwind)

Source: `apps/docs/content/docs/platforms/uniwind-bare.mdx`

In addition to React Native Web (`apps/native-playground`), the same Apple-inspired design system powers **Bare React Native** applications running directly on Android and iOS devices. Bare React Native bundles through **Metro** and compiles Tailwind CSS v4 utilities for native view trees using **Uniwind**.

## Architecture comparison

| Layer | React Native Web (RNW) | Bare React Native (Mobile) |
| ----- | ---------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Bundler | Vite (`vite-plugin-rnw`, `uniwind/vite`) | Metro (`@react-native/metro-config`, `uniwind/metro`) |
| Runtime | Browser DOM (simulated primitives) | Native Android & iOS view hierarchies |
| Tokens | `@package/ui/tokens.css` (CSS variables) | Same `@package/ui/tokens.css`, compiled by Uniwind at build time |
| Components | `@package/ui-native` (`Pressable`, `View`, `Text`) | Same `@package/ui-native` primitives and source exports |
| Scaffolding | `universal create <name> --framework native` | `universal create <name> --framework uniwind-bare` |

## Scaffolding a new bare project

Create a runnable bare React Native project configured with Metro, Uniwind, and Tailwind CSS v4:

```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli create my-mobile-app --framework uniwind-bare
```

Or using the alias:

```bash
npx @next-mmo/universal-cli create my-mobile-app --framework native-bare
```

This scaffolds:
- `metro.config.js` configured with `withUniwindConfig`
- `babel.config.js` with standard React Native presets
- `src/index.css` importing Tailwind v4 and Uniwind
- `index.js` registering the root component with `AppRegistry`
- `src/App.tsx` rendering styled native components
- `universal.json` pre-configured to add `@package/ui-native` components

## Metro bundler configuration

In a bare React Native project, Uniwind hooks into Metro via `withUniwindConfig`:

```js
// metro.config.js
const { getDefaultConfig, mergeConfig } = require('@react-native/metro-config');
const { withUniwindConfig } = require('uniwind/metro');

const config = mergeConfig(getDefaultConfig(__dirname), {
  /* custom metro configuration */
});

module.exports = withUniwindConfig(config, {
  cssEntryFile: './src/index.css',
});
```

Uniwind parses Tailwind classes in JSX during bundling and resolves them into optimized native style objects.

## CSS entry and design tokens

The CSS entry file (`src/index.css`) imports Tailwind v4, Uniwind, and the shared design tokens:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "uniwind";
@import "@package/ui/src/styles/tokens.css";
```

In source-distributed projects (via `universal init` and `universal add`), the token file is generated locally under `src/lib/universal/ui/styles/tokens.css`.

## Component parity on bare runtime

Components in `@package/ui-native` (and source-distributed components) are crafted strictly from standard React Native primitives:

- **Buttons & Pressables**: Built with React Native's `Pressable` and `Text`, with pressed state feedback using `active:` opacity utilities.
- **Form Controls**: `Input` wraps `TextInput` with token-aware placeholders; `Switch` provides a pure native toggle.
- **Overlay Sheets**: Because native has no DOM portals, overlay components (`Dialog`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Select`) render using React Native's `Modal` component over dimmed backdrops.
- **Animations**: `Skeleton` uses React Native `Animated` loops instead of CSS keyframes.
- **Icons**: Simple glyphs (✓, ⌄, ×) are used to avoid hard dependencies on native SVG packages.

## Theme and dark mode

Theme transitions are managed directly through Uniwind:

```tsx

// Toggle between light and dark modes
Uniwind.setTheme('dark');
Uniwind.setTheme('light');
```

Uniwind dynamically switches CSS custom properties and re-renders affected native components without reloading the bundle.
